name: OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) - Reference
command: # Map each API finding to its OWASP API risk and the card that exploits it
description: Reference index of the OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023). For each risk: the one-line test approach and the card in this library that exploits it. Gives a home to the categories the CWES M18 lab teaches through its UI (BFLA, BOPLA, business flows, unsafe consumption) that don't reduce to a single copy-paste command.
notes:
OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) — test approach → covering card:

API1 Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA): swap an object ID (userId, orderId, GUID) for another user's and see if the API returns it. → api-bola-sequential-enum, idor-api.
API2 Broken Authentication: weak/absent auth on token issue, no rate limit on login/OTP, forgeable/weak JWT. → auth-password-bruteforce-ffuf, api-ffuf-json-bruteforce, auth-session-token-forge.
API3 Broken Object Property Level Authorization (BOPLA): send extra/hidden JSON properties the client shouldn't set (mass assignment) or read fields you shouldn't (excessive data exposure). → mass-assignment.
API4 Unrestricted Resource Consumption: no size/type/rate limit on uploads or expensive calls → DoS, cost, exe upload. → api-unrestricted-resource-consumption.
API5 Broken Function Level Authorization (BFLA): call an admin/privileged function (often just a different HTTP verb or /admin path) as a low-priv user. Test method: replay an action with a lower-role token; change GET→PUT/DELETE. (No single command — enumerate roles vs endpoints.)
API6 Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows: automate a business flow the app assumes is manual (bulk-buy limited stock, mass-create accounts, scalping). Test method: script the flow and check for missing anti-automation controls.
API7 Server Side Request Forgery: API fetches a user-supplied URL without validation. → ssrf-identify, ssrf-blind, ssrf-exploit.
API8 Security Misconfiguration: verbose errors, CORS, missing headers, injection via misconfig. → api-enum-abuse; injection cards (sqli/xss/ssti).
API9 Improper Inventory Management: old/undocumented API versions (v1 vs v2), staging/debug hosts still live. → api-version-enum.
API10 Unsafe Consumption of APIs: the target trusts a third-party API's data without validation — poison the upstream/redirect it. Test method: MITM/replace the consumed API's response and observe blind trust.

Workflow: enumerate endpoints and roles first (Swagger/OpenAPI, /docs, api-version-enum), map each endpoint to the risks above, then reach for the specific card.

recommended.note: Start by mapping versions/endpoints (API9) before testing risks.
API1 BOLA is the most common and highest-yield API bug.
API4 - the one category with a concrete upload exploit.
